title: The Regime-Consistent Measurement Principle (RCMP): A Methodological Framework for Multi-Scale Physics
description: Introduces the Regime-Consistent Measurement Principle (RCMP), a methodology that requires interpreting observables via variables most directly coupled to the physical driver within the operative regime, with explicit cross-regime transformation and uncertainty propagation. The paper formalizes five core principles (driver proximity, regime tagging, proxy accounting, coordinate humility, and cross-validation) and demonstrates the framework on galaxy rotation curves, separating intra-galaxy from inter-galaxy effects and resolving an apparent low-acceleration scatter discrepancy in the SPARC dataset.

centripetal_acceleration.description: Defines the observed centripetal acceleration from the rotation curve, used as an L2 derived quantity in the RCMP hierarchy for galaxy dynamics.

scatter_ratio_metric.description: Operational definition of the per-point scatter ratio used to compare intra-galaxy variability between dwarf and spiral classes in the low-acceleration regime.

key_results.main_finding: Applying RCMP to SPARC rotation curves shows dwarfs have 1.27× higher per-point scatter than spirals in the low-g regime (p = 0.02) while per-galaxy median responses are statistically indistinguishable (p = 0.47), separating intra-galaxy variability from inter-galaxy physics.
parameters_tested: effects of distance and inclination uncertainties

kill_criteria: KC1: Reproduce the published RCMP workflow on SPARC or successor high-quality rotation-curve datasets with improved systematics; if, in the low-acceleration regime, dwarf and spiral per-galaxy median residuals exhibit a statistically significant (>3σ) class-level offset, contradicting the paper’s main finding, RCMP’s regime-separation claim is falsified.

KC2: In at least three independent multi-regime domains with unambiguous driver identification (e.g., galaxy dynamics, plasma transport, and climate reanalysis), RCMP-compliant analyses yield consistently worse out-of-sample predictive accuracy or larger calibrated residuals than naive mixed-regime analyses by >10% with p < 0.01; this would refute RCMP’s utility.

KC3: For two or more datasets within a single regime, independent proxy chains targeting the same driver (e.g., acceleration inferred via distinct calibrations) disagree beyond the propagated uncertainty budgets after documented systematics are corrected, indicating RCMP’s proxy accounting fails to bound uncertainty.

KC4: Vary physically admissible coordinate choices across multiple datasets and regimes; if all inferences and uncertainty estimates remain invariant (differences consistent with zero at p < 0.01), the practical necessity of RCMP’s coordinate humility principle is invalidated.

KC5: Demonstrate across at least three systems spanning distinct regimes that direct cross-regime comparisons without explicit transformations reproduce RCMP-transformed results within 1σ for all primary inferences; this would negate the need for RCMP’s explicit cross-regime mapping requirement.
